aliases.label: David Hopper (dock sales, PPL)
aliases.rationale: Confirmed via golden-master validation against SALES COMPLETE.xlsx (tag A1): QuickBooks PO field records the surname ("Hopper"), Infinium OHDESC records only the first name ("David") for the same recurring dock-sale customer. No text-similarity rule can bridge a surname and a first name that share no characters.

aliases.label: Midwest Fabrication (dock sales, PPL)
aliases.rationale: QuickBooks sometimes records the full name ("Midwest Fabrication") while Infinium records the abbreviation ("Midwest Fab") -- no shared token, so no text-similarity rule could ever bridge "FABRICATION" vs "FAB" (ratio ~0.43, well under the 0.84 near-miss threshold). "MIDWEST" itself is not included since it already matches exactly on both sides; only the divergent variant is aliased.

aliases.label: Jerry Wood (dock sales, PPL)
aliases.rationale: Infinium often records this recurring dock-sale customer as a glued reference code rather than the plain name -- e.g. "JWOOD7060" (now split by the letter/digit tokenizer fix into "JWOOD" + a dropped reference number) or "JERRYWOOD" with no space. None of these share a token with QuickBooks' plain "JERRY WOOD" without this alias. Note: a glued form with an unrelated word fused on with no digit boundary at all (e.g. "POJERRYWOOD") still cannot be split by the tokenizer and stays outside this alias -- that specific pattern would need a deeper tokenizer change, not just an alias entry. Revised: excluded the bare first name "JERRY" after confirming it also appears in two other, unrelated dock-sale customers in this same dataset ("Jerry Potter" and "Jerry - Gibbs Electric", both also $225) -- too generic to safely alias on its own. Revised again: added the literal glued form "POJERRYWOOD" (Infinium invoice 221339, 4/27/2026) after finding that leaving it out let the alias resolve to a DIFFERENT candidate (invoice 21017 "JWOOD7060", 3/03/2026) with false confidence -- both are $225 and either could plausibly be the true counterpart to the QuickBooks 6/4/2026 row, so this stays a genuine, correctly-unresolved ambiguity between the two until a person confirms which one it actually is.

aliases.label: Amarillo Bolt (dock sales, PPL)
aliases.rationale: Recurring dock-sale customer referenced with inconsistent abbreviations across systems -- e.g. "ABOLT184225" (glued reference code, now split by the letter/digit tokenizer fix), or shorthand like "AMA BOLT" / "Amarillo BLT". Deliberately does NOT include the bare word "AMARILLO": the company is based in Amarillo, TX, so many unrelated vendor names in this ledger may also contain "Amarillo" (confirmed one such case already exists: "AMARILLO TRUCK&TRAILER-QUENTIN", a different business). Aliasing the bare city name would risk merging unrelated vendors; only the bolt-specific terms are linked.
